Action to perform: Describe a trait as a quality (Q) of an entity (E), a formalism widely used to describe the traits of organisms.
Describe the sampling protocols (of the entity)
Record a unique identifier for the sample (if tracked across multiple measurements).
Describe the measurement methods (of the quality)
Use acknowledged standards when available.
Identify each replicate measurement
Record data at the finest resolution possible, that is, one record per trait measurement, which can even include the within-individual or within-organ level
Homogenize units
Record the date and time of each sampling/measurement
Report the geolocation of each sampling/measurement (if necessary)
Specify the full scientific name (if identified at the species level: binomial name, including genus and species, in Latin).
If taxon identified at the species level: indicate the name of the author(s) of the species name (authority)
Document the taxonomic reference used [see also B.1.2]
Provide a unique taxonomic identifier from the chosen taxonomic reference for each taxon [see also B.2.4].
Keep the original taxon names used during data collection, if they differ from the standardized names used in the final dataset.
Document relevant infraspecific taxonomic rank (subspecies, variety, cultivar, genotype ID, accession number...) and provide its identifier if possible
Document relevant higher taxonomic information (e.g., family, order)
Document any relevant information on the taxon that provides biological context.
Document any relevant information about the state of the sampled organism that could influence trait values.
Indicate the spatial organization of the observational or experimental design, including whether the data were measured in a glasshouse, a common garden, or in the field
Define the environmental variables reported
Describe the sampling protocol for environmental variables
Describe the measurement method for environmental variables
Specify the units of the environmental variables reported
Refer to a standard (if available)
Indicate the spatial scale of the measurements
Specify the origin of the environmental variables (measured locally vs. extracted from databases)
Identity of the origin of the measurement: experimenter(s), name of project, grants...
Provide contacts
Cite publications that have used the data

Category2: B.1) Format and structure the data

Action to perform: Store data in a non-proprietary, machine-readable format (e.g., .txt, or .csv)
Include as much information as possible within the tables
Choose a structure for the data
In each table, generate a unique identifier ("primary key") for each row
If following a relational database structure, refer to the primary key of the extensions within the core observation table
Rely on a standard to define variable/column names (if possible).
Describe precisely the variables not found in standards (when documenting the general metadata).
Standardize trait names and methods by mapping them to persistent identifiers from community-accepted ontologies.
Standardize taxonomic names by mapping them to persistent identifiers from a community-accepted source (cf. A.2.3)
Standardise environmental measurements by referencing relevant ontologies or thesauri (cf. A.3.5)
Favour algorithmic over manual restructuration
Use a version control system
Share the code used to restructure data
Associate a usage license to the scripts

Category2: C.1) Publish a metadata file in a standard format

Action to perform: Use a community-approved metadata standard
Publish the metadata to a searchable repository or catalog.

Category2: C.2) Publish a rich metadata file

Action to perform: Make a general description of the dataset (title, originators, abstract, key words)
Describe the data content (trait and taxonomic coverage, etc.) and structure (tables, variables, relationships)
Document the quality control procedures applied [cf. Section E]
Provide information on accessibility (repositories, persistent identifier, license usage) [cf. Section D]
Disseminate the information about the data publication (and possibly write a data paper)

Category2: D.1) Preserve and license the data package

Action to perform: Archive data in a long-term repository committed to FAIR practices, queriable by both humans and machines, and associate its metadata.
Upload metadata together with the data
Assign a persistent identifier (DOI) to the dataset.
Specify reusability conditions with a clear usage license

Category2: D.2) Preserve and license the processing scripts

Action to perform: Preserve the processing code/scripts to a repository (with a DOI and license).
Check data structure
Check numeric variables for outliers and plausible ranges.
Check units for homogeneity across the dataset.
Check non-numeric variables (e.g., taxon names, identifiers) for misspellings and consistency.
Ensure that URLs pointing to external references are functional
Ensure reproducibility of the quality control and correction procedures
Proofread the metadata files and control for errors.
Verify the published data package matches the intended release, and pay particular attention to control the presence of DOIs and licenses.
